question: How can neural network training algorithms (update rules, tuning protocols, schedules, data selection) be compared reliably, so that real speedups can be identified and a state of the art established?
hypothesis: A competitive time-to-result benchmark on fixed hardware, with multiple fixed workloads, randomized held-out workload variants, and explicit accounting for hyperparameter tuning, resolves the three challenges (when training is done, workload sensitivity, fair tuning) that make current optimizer comparisons unreliable.
contributions: Articulate the challenges of benchmarking training algorithms with concrete experiments (Section 2).

Introduce the AlgoPerf: Training Algorithms benchmark: time-to-result on 8 fixed workloads on fixed hardware, with target setting, held-out randomized workloads, external and self-tuning rulesets, and performance-profile scoring (Section 4).

Construct baselines from eight optimizers (AdamW, NadamW, Heavy Ball, Nesterov, LAMB, Adafactor, SAM (w. Adam), Distributed Shampoo) with search spaces, setting a provisional state of the art (Section 7).
Build 24 workload variants (3 per fixed workload) and show the need for research on hyperparameter transfer (Section 6).

method.summary: A competitive time-to-result benchmark: a submission defines four API functions (init_optimizer_state, update_params, data_selection, get_batch_size) and optionally a hyperparameter search space, and is timed on wall clock until it reaches validation and test targets on 8 fixed workloads (plus 8 held-out workload variants used as a penalty). Targets are set by tuning four optimizers with 200 quasirandom trials per workload, rerunning the best 20 times. Eight baseline optimizers are scored with performance profiles integrated to a 0-1 benchmark score. Section 2 supports the design with small experiments on stride, extra batch norm, Pre/Post-LN, hyperparameter sensitivity, search-space and tuning-goal effects.
method.task: benchmarking training algorithms (optimizers, schedules, regularisation, data selection) for time to a target out-of-sample error across image classification, speech recognition, machine translation, MRI reconstruction, click-through rate prediction and molecular property prediction

datasets.name: Criteo 1TB Click Logs
datasets.split: first 23 days train; first half of day 24 test; second half of day 24 validation
datasets.preprocessing: 13 numerical features log-transformed; 26 categorical features hashed into one embedding table; training files of 5,000,000 lines shuffled; metric is sigmoid binary cross entropy not AUC; budget allows about 60% of an epoch

datasets.name: fastMRI (single-coil knee)
datasets.size: 34,742 training slices (973 volumes); validation set of 7,135 slices (199 volumes) split into 3,554 validation (first 100 files) and 3,581 test slices (final 99 files)
datasets.split: official validation split roughly in half into validation and test
datasets.preprocessing: fixed random column mask, 4x down-sampling, inverse Fourier transform, normalisation by mean and std

datasets.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012) with ImageNet-v2 test
datasets.split: ILSVRC 2012 train and validation; ImageNet-v2 as test
datasets.source: Deng et al. 2009; Recht et al. 2019
datasets.preprocessing: random crop and flip for training, center crop for eval, inputs in [0,1]; RandAugment and mixup used for ViT but not ResNet

datasets.name: LibriSpeech
datasets.size: 960 hours of raw audio training (train-clean-100, train-clean-360, train-other-500); 5567 validation examples
datasets.preprocessing: drop examples with audio length > 320k or target length > 256; log-mel spectrograms; SentencePiece vocab 1024

datasets.name: OGBG-MOLPCBA
datasets.size: 350,343 training examples; 43,793 each in validation and test (text says 'the train and validation splits both contain 43,793 examples')
datasets.preprocessing: dynamic batching with max nodes = BatchSize*AvgNumNodes and max edges = 2*BatchSize*AvgNumEdges

datasets.name: WMT 2017 De->En (train), WMT 2014 De->En (dev/test)
datasets.size: about 5.9 million parallel sentence pairs; validation 3000 and test 3003 sentence pairs (newstest2014)
datasets.split: train WMT17; validation = WMT14 dev; test = newstest2014
datasets.preprocessing: SentencePiece 32k shared vocab; sentences > 256 tokens removed; no monolingual data or augmentation

models.name: DLRMsmall (Criteo 1TB)
models.architecture: DLRM: one 4M-entry embedding table of dim 128; dense MLP 512-256-128; cross-interaction; top MLP 1024-1024-512-256-1; ReLU; dropout after the 512 layer

models.name: U-Net (fastMRI)
models.architecture: U-Net, 32 channels, 4 down-sampling conv blocks and 4 up-sampling blocks, dropout default 0.0

models.name: ResNet-50 (ImageNet)
models.architecture: ResNet-50 per He et al. 2016a Sec 4.1, ghost batch norm virtual batch size 64, final BN scale in each residual block initialised to zero

models.name: ViT S/16 (ImageNet)
models.architecture: Vision Transformer S/16, width 384, depth 12, MLP dim 1536, 6 heads, 16x16 patches, no regularisation, light2 augmentation (mixup alpha 0.2, RandAugment 2 layers magnitude 15)

models.name: Conformer (LibriSpeech)
models.architecture: 4-layer Conformer, encoder dim 512, Xavier uniform init, CTC loss, greedy decoding

models.name: DeepSpeech (LibriSpeech)
models.architecture: DeepSpeech variant with residual connections, dropout, layer norm, SpecAugment; conv subsampling by 4, 6 bi-LSTM layers, 3 feed-forward layers, dim 512, batch norm in LSTM/FF layers, CTC loss

models.name: GNN (OGBG)
models.architecture: Jraph GNN: linear embedding size 256, global features 128, 5 message passing steps, update fns are 1-layer FC (256, layer norm, ReLU, dropout default 0.1), LeCun normal init

models.name: Transformer-big (WMT)
models.architecture: Transformer-big (Vaswani 2017) with modifications: 6 encoder and 6 decoder layers, model dim 1024, hidden dim 4096, 16 heads, shared embeddings; Pre-LN in base workload; default label smoothing 0.1 and dropout 0.1

models.name: Wide ResNet 28-10 (CIFAR-10, Section 2)
models.architecture: 3 groups of 4 residual blocks, 2 conv layers each; default strides 1x1, 2x2, 2x2; variant sets group-3 stride to 1x1 (final dense layer fan-in grows 81x, 640x10 to 51840x10)

models.name: ResNetV2-200 with extra batch norm (Section 2)
models.architecture: 200-layer ResNetV2 with BN added after every residual connection (each block returns BN(x+F(x))), all BN scales initialised to 1, virtual batch size 64

training.objective: per workload: cross-entropy (Criteo, ImageNet, OGBG, WMT), L1 (fastMRI), CTC (LibriSpeech); evaluation metrics CE, SSIM, error rate, WER, mAP, BLEU
training.optimizer: Baselines: AdamW, NadamW, Nesterov, Heavy Ball, LAMB, Adafactor, SAM (w. Adam), Distributed Shampoo. Target-setting used AdamW, NadamW, Nesterov, Heavy Ball.
training.lr: tuned: target-setting Base LR Log[1e-5,1e-1] (AdamW, NadamW), Log[1e-3,10] (Heavy Ball, Nesterov); baseline Log[1e-4,1e-2] (Adam-family) and Log[1e-1,10] (Heavy Ball, Nesterov) (Tables 8, 12)
training.lr_schedule: AdamW/NadamW/LAMB/Adafactor/SAM/Shampoo: linear warmup + cosine decay. Heavy Ball/Nesterov: linear warmup + linear decay + constant (decay factor {1e-2,1e-3}, decay steps 0.9 in baselines). Formulas in Appendix A.1.
training.warmup: target-setting {2%,5%,10%} for Adam-family, 5% for momentum methods; baselines fixed 5% linear warmup from 0.0
training.batch_size: chosen per workload by the submission (get_batch_size); not tabulated in the paper. WMT: batch size 128 corresponds to about 280K tokens each on source and target side.
training.steps: inferred: max steps per workload equal Table 28 'Steps' row (reading from Table 28): Criteo 10,667; fastMRI 36,189; ResNet-50 186,667; ViT 186,667; Conformer 133,333; DeepSpeech 80,000; OGBG 80,000; WMT 133,333. Target-setting used 0.75x these budgets.
training.weight_decay: tuned: target-setting Log[1e-5,1] (Adam-family), Log[1e-7,1e-2] (momentum); baseline Log[5e-3,1] (AdamW/NadamW), Log[1e-7,1e-5] (Heavy Ball/Nesterov)
training.regularisation: label smoothing {0.0,0.1,0.2} in target-setting, {0.1,0.2} in baselines; dropout; aux dropout; only on workloads that support them
training.hardware: official benchmark system 8x NVIDIA V100 16GB; most baseline tuning runs on Google TPUs
training.compute: Table 15 estimates: one hyperparameter on all 16 workloads 232.23 h; scoring a submission 1161.13 h; tuning a submission 23,222.61 h (external tuning ruleset, 8xV100 hours). Combined fixed-workload runtime budget targeted at 100 hours.
training.wall_clock: Max runtimes in seconds (Table 7): Criteo 7703; fastMRI 8859; ResNet-50 63,008; ViT 77,520; Conformer 101,780; DeepSpeech 92,509; OGBG 18,477; WMT 48,151. Self-tuning ruleset allows 3x.
training.seeds: target-setting: best trial rerun with 20 seeds; external tuning scoring: 5 independent studies of 20 trials each (100 trials)

other.tuning_search: quasirandom search (Bousquet 2017); target-setting 200 trials per algorithm per workload; external tuning 20 trials per study x 5 studies
other.target_setting_rule: validation target = median best validation over 20 reruns; test target = worst test error among the 10 reruns that hit the validation target
other.baseline_timing: each algorithm (except Distributed Shampoo) run for 20% of steps on the official system, extrapolated, averaged over two machines
other.section2_experiments: Wide ResNet: Nesterov vs AdamW with a simple LR sweep and cosine decay (details limited); Pre-LN vs Post-LN: 100 random-search trials per optimizer, 133K steps each, bootstrap sample size 20; Phi(H): 100 quasirandom settings, one run each, 8 workloads; AdamW narrow vs broad: 100 quasirandom points each, simulated tuning with T trials over 1000 simulations; Fig 4: step budgets 186,666 vs 233,333, 100 trials, 20 seeds for best trial
other.optlist_baselines: 20 configurations built greedily round-robin across workloads from the top configs of the 200-trial searches

inference.decoding: WMT: beam search beam size 4, length penalty 0.6; LibriSpeech Conformer: greedy decoding
inference.samples: n/a for the generative models; see training.seeds

metrics.name: time-to-result
metrics.definition: wall-clock time to first reach the validation and test targets on a workload; infinity if not reached within the max runtime

metrics.name: benchmark score B
metrics.definition: integral of the performance profile rho(tau) from tau=1 to r_max=4, normalised by r_max-1; performance ratio = time of submission / best time on that workload

metrics.name: Phi(H)
metrics.definition: min over h in H of max over workloads of |val(w,h)-val_H(w)|/val_H(w); best worst-case relative degradation from sharing one hyperparameter setting across workloads

metrics.name: workload metrics
metrics.definition: CE (Criteo), SSIM (fastMRI), error rate (ImageNet), WER (LibriSpeech), mAP (OGBG), BLEU (sacreBLEU, WMT)

eval.protocol: External tuning: 20 trials drawn quasirandomly per study, 5 studies, per workload median of 5 study times (hyperparameters selected by time to validation target, scored by time to test target). Self-tuning: no tuning trials, 3x runtime, 5 studies. Held-out workload variants penalise submissions that fail them (Section 4.5.3); baselines in the paper ignore the held-out criterion.

limits: Authors concede the target-setting procedure needed manual trial-and-error on search spaces, uses 200 trials (not a valid submission), and yields targets that are generally not state-of-the-art error rates (Section 8.1).

Randomized workload variants were designed by hand (only three per workload), may not be mutually distinct, and often repeat similar changes such as activation swaps; hyperparameter transfer is not predicted by any theory (Sections 6.2, 8.2, 8.4).

Only one hardware class (8x V100) and one batch-size regime; relative optimizer performance may vary with batch size and scale. Baselines were mostly run on TPUs and extrapolated from 20% of steps on GPUs (Sections 7.2, 8.4).

Heavy Ball and Nesterov failures reflect the box search spaces, not the update rules; Distributed Shampoo could not be run on the official system and has a step-budget advantage; the authors' Adafactor was slower than expected (Sections 7.2, 7.3, 8.3).
Three of eight workloads (Criteo, fastMRI, OGBG) are data-pipeline-bound on the official system, favoring more expensive optimizers (Section 7.2).
Baselines ignore the held-out workload criterion; the scores depend on the full set of baselines in the performance profile, so they are relative, not absolute (Sections 4.5, 7.3).

Submissions are limited by the API (no model parallelism, no K-FAC-style architectural access, random search only for external tuning, JAX/PyTorch only); no language modelling, video or image generation workloads (Section 8.4).

Section 2 experiments are small: Phi uses one run per hyperparameter setting; the Wide ResNet and Extra-BN experiments are single-sweep demonstrations with few details; DeepSpeech validation target expected to change from 0.1162 to 0.111825 before the call for submissions (Appendix D.4.3).
Compute cost of scoring (about 1161 machine-hours) is a barrier; the benchmark is all-or-nothing across workloads (Section 8.4).

terms.definition: wall-clock time for a run to first reach workload-specific validation and test error targets; infinity if the maximum runtime is exceeded
a dataset (including preprocessing), model, and loss function, along with a target defined using some evaluation metric
a plot of the fraction of workloads where a given method is within some ratio of the best per-workload training time
20 quasirandom trials from a submission-supplied workload-agnostic search space (or a fixed OptList), repeated in 5 studies, median per-workload time scored
no user-defined hyperparameters or external tuning; all adaptation happens on the clock, with 3x the runtime budget
a fixed list of 20 hyperparameter points sampled without replacement in lieu of a search space (after Metz et al. 2020 'learned optimizer list')
a concrete workload variant sampled after submissions are frozen from a randomized workload (a distribution over three hand-designed variants of a fixed workload)
the best worst-case relative performance degradation from using a single shared hyperparameter setting in H instead of per-workload tuning

code.snippet: r_{s,w} = t_{s,w} / min_{s in S} t_{s,w};  rho_s(tau) = (1/n) |{w : r_{s,w} <= tau}|;  B_s = 1/(r_max - 1) * integral_1^{r_max} rho_s(tau) dtau, r_max = 4
Phi(H) = min_{h in H} max_w | val(w,h) - val_H(w) | / val_H(w)
LR(t) = BaseLR * t/WarmupSteps for t <= WarmupSteps; else BaseLR/2 * (1 + cos(pi * (t-WarmupSteps)/(NumSteps-WarmupSteps)))
